title: Shopify opens its catalog up to more AI agents
key_facts: Shopify announced on Tuesday 13 Oct 2026 that it will let shoppers configure their own AI agents to purchase products for them (The Verge).
This gives more agents access to over a billion listings in Shopify's catalog, which includes items on and off Shopify storefronts.
In September Shopify announced a partnership with Meta so its Muse agent could browse and buy; now shoppers can use any agent without a partnership integration.
Customers connect an agent to their account on Shop, a Shopify-owned platform that tracks orders and packages; checkout is one-click Shop Pay inside the conversation with the agent.
Shopify markets the feature as a "personal shopper" that people can give rules, such as budget guardrails or fast shipping only; buyers must approve each purchase.

The Verge says e-commerce is a battleground for AI and notes an ongoing fight between Amazon and AI companies such as Perplexity, and more recently Meta's Muse, over whether agents may shop for customers.
quote_evidence: In September, Shopify announced it was partnering with Meta to allow its Muse agent to browse and purchase items on a human’s behalf; now, shoppers can use any agent without a partnership integration.
Shopify announced Tuesday it will let shoppers configure their AI agents to purchase products on their behalf, giving more agents access to over a billion listings in Shopify’s catalog.
why_it_matters_hint: Shoppers can use the AI agent they prefer to buy from Shopify's catalog, with limits and approval, in a wider fight over agent shopping.
notes: Full text read. The article says agents "will soon" be able to shop; no launch date is given.
